newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philex sees 1997 net at 507 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Philex sees 1997 net at 507 mln pesos.

text.p: Philex Mining Corp, the country's largest gold mining company, expects to make a net profit of 507 million pesos this year, company chairman Gerard Brimo said on Tuesday.

Increased output of 341,000 ounces of gold from three mine fields will help earnings, Brimo told Reuters in a telephone interview. Last year, the company produced 181,083 ounces last year from two mines.
Brimo said the company projected the price of gold to rise to $365 per ounce from the current $340.
Philex posted a net income of 1.4 billion pesos in 1996 including extraordinaries compared with 369 million pesos in 1995, Brimo said.
The extraodinary gains included 1.35 billion from the sale of Philex shares in CityTrust Banking Corp, the company earlier said in a statement.

Another one-time gain of 900 million pesos was recorded from the initial public offering of its Canadian gold unit, Philex Gold Inc which was listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange on October 26, 1996, it said. Philex Mining now owns 81.8 percent of Philex Gold.

To take advantage of the high extraordinary gains, Brimo said the company provided for a 998 million-peso writedown in the value of its Padcal copper-gold mine assets and its deferred mining and oil exploration costs.
Brimo said Philex Mining's share of the income from its overseas subsidiary amounted to 149 million pesos for 1996.

The company's Bulawan mine in central Philippines, under the control of Philex Gold, is projected to increase its output this year to 165,000 ounces of gold at a cash cost of $180 an ounce versus last year's 90,083 ounces of gold at a cash cost of $199 an ounce, he said. The Bulawam mine had its first year of commercial operations in 1996.
"The Bulawan mine is considered to be a low cost producer by world standards and should remain profitable even at the current low price of gold," Brimo said.

Philex Gold will bring into production in the second quarter of 1997 its second gold mine, Sibutad, located in the province of Zamboanga del Norte in southern Philippines. Its initial output is projected at 35,000 ounces at a cash cost of $190 per ounce, the company said.

Gold and copper mine Padcal, which is directly under Philex Mining, is forecast to be profitable in 1997 after turning out an operating loss of 148 million pesos due to operational problems at the underground mine site.

Pacdal, located in Benguet province, northern Philippine, is estimated to have an output of 21 million kg of copper and 4.4 million grams of gold in 1997, 30 percent and 55 percent higher respectively than in 1996, the company said.
Brimo added shareholders approved last Monday a 50 percent stock dividend and an increase in the authorised capital stock to 5.0 billion pesos from 2.0 billion pesos.
